member.name: T:Orchard.Mirror.Audio.Windows.FdkAacEldDecoder
member.summary: Decodes the device's AAC-ELD access units to 16-bit stereo PCM through libfdk-aac.

remarks.para: Windows has no AAC-ELD decoder of its own — Media Foundation's AAC decoder covers LC and HE only — so something has to supply one. libfdk-aac is used here rather than FFmpeg or FAAD2 because it is not copyleft, which is what ADR 0014 §4 actually requires of the media path.

This deviates from ADR 0014 §6, which says the decoder will be Orchard's own. That decision was taken when no other non-copyleft option had been identified. The deviation is deliberate and needs the ADR amended or this replaced; see docs/orchard-mirror/AUDIO_2026-08-02.md. Note that writing our own would not change the AAC patent position, which is the same either way.
The type deliberately exposes nothing of libfdk-aac, so replacing it later is a one-file change.

member.name: T:Orchard.Mirror.Audio.Windows.WaveOutRenderer
member.summary: Plays 16-bit stereo PCM through the default Windows output device.

remarks.para: Buffers are small and few on purpose. This audio accompanies a mirrored screen, so a deep queue does not protect against anything a viewer wants — it just puts the sound further behind the picture. The queue is a fixed ring, and when every buffer is still playing the incoming frame is dropped rather than waited on, which keeps the decode thread from becoming the thing that stalls the session.

waveOut rather than WASAPI: at 10 ms per frame the extra latency is small, and the API cannot deadlock the caller. If lip-sync ever needs the last few milliseconds, this type is the only thing that has to change.

member.name: F:Orchard.Mirror.Audio.Windows.WaveOutRenderer.BufferCount
